title: Latency spike during quantized model swap — postmortem and runbook updates
content:
Summary:

On 2025-11-03 we observed a rapid p95 latency increase for one of our canary pools during a scheduled model variant swap (hosted-api, model: redwood-rm-l2-quant-v2). The canary was receiving 5% of production traffic. The increase impacted only the canary nodes and did not cross the global latency alert thresholds, so customer-facing requests remained within SLA. Root cause was a mismatch between model metadata (quantized=true) and the actually packaged weight format; the serving runtime selected an unoptimized float execution path and disabled certain fused attention kernels, causing large batching inefficiencies and a 2–4x p95 regression for short-sequence workloads.

Impact:
- Affected pool: canary-us-west-2-quant (5% traffic)
- Duration: ~09:22:00 UTC — 10:03:00 UTC (41 minutes)
- Symptoms: p50 ~ unchanged (+10%), p95 ↑ 2–4x, tail CPU/GPU utilization spikes on canary nodes, increased queue length and request requeueing; roughly 3% of canary requests experienced >2s latency (normally <300ms). No customer-facing SLA breaches because canary traffic was isolated and global alerts didn’t fire.

How it was detected:
- 09:23 UTC: telemetry anomaly detection flagged CPU utilization on canary nodes as >90% for 5m.
- 09:25 UTC: on-call (Ethan) saw p95 latency alert for canary dashboard (internal threshold) and Slack alert for increased error budget burn on canary route.
- 09:26 UTC: initial triage showed that only the canary variant was affected; other pools normal.

Initial mitigation actions (actions taken during on-call):
1) 09:28 UTC — Pause rollout (Traffic split -> 0% to canary variant). This prevented further users from hitting the bad variant.
2) 09:31 UTC — Scale up canary nodes by +20% to reduce queueing while debugging (temporary relief).
3) 09:35 UTC — Rollback to previous model variant on canary nodes (deployed previous immutable model manifest). Traffic was switched back to previous model at 09:41 UTC.
4) 09:45 UTC — Drain and reprovision canary nodes to clear stubborn KV cache state.
5) 10:03 UTC — Observed p95 returning to baseline; incident declared contained.

Timeline (detailed):
- 09:20 UTC — Automated rollout job completed image+artifact publication for redwood-rm-l2-quant-v2; canary traffic ramp started (target 5%).
- 09:22 UTC — First internal CPU spike/telemetry anomaly on canary nodes.
- 09:25 UTC — On-call notified and began triage.
- 09:27 UTC — Runtime logs show repeated entries from kernel_selector: "selected_unoptimized_path=true reason=quant_flag_mismatch" and "disabled_fused_attention=true".
- 09:30 UTC — Confirmed mismatch between model manifest metadata (metadata.quantized=true) and weight file header (weights indicate mixed precision / incomplete quant blocks).
- 09:33 UTC — CI artifact verification absent checksum for quant blocks; build pipeline published artifact without the expected verification step.
- 09:35 UTC — Rollback initiated.
- 09:41 UTC — Rollback complete and traffic reverted.
- 10:03 UTC — System stabilized, alerting returned to baseline.

Root cause analysis:
1) Packaging bug in CI (build/packager v1.12.0, build 17422) that omitted final quant block assembly in ~1 of 25 artifact builds due to a race between weight-sharding and quantization job. The artifact manifest was still marked quantized=true.
2) Serving runtime kernel selector relies primarily on model metadata flags (metadata.quantized) to select optimized kernels and code paths. When metadata indicates quantized and the runtime cannot validate weight internals quickly, it takes the safer route of enabling float fallback but still disables some fused kernels (to avoid silent correctness issues). This combination resulted in significant de-optimized execution for short-sequence workloads (we make heavy use of fused attention for p50/p95 improvements).
3) Monitoring and alerting gaps: our alerting rules were global and not configured to escalate per-canary pool at the thresholds we use for production. The canary-specific p95 alert existed but had a higher threshold, so automated pageing did not occur immediately.

Why this caused a latency spike (technical detail):
- Fused attention kernels are the primary latency optimization for our short-sequence path. When disabled, the runtime falls back to multiple kernel launches per attention block, increasing kernel launch overhead and preventing efficient batching of tiny requests.
- Quantized artifacts with missing quant blocks cause the runtime to detect an inconsistency and enable conservative safety checks, preventing use of fast int8 kernels.
- The canary workload had predominantly short sequences (median len=32 tokens) which are disproportionately impacted by kernel launch overhead; this produced a heavy tail.

What went well:
- Canary isolation prevented customer-facing SLA breaches.
- Rollout pause and quick rollback were effective — system stabilized within ~40 minutes.
- Runtime logs provided a clear high-signal debug hint (kernel_selector message).

What went poorly:
- CI packaging race allowed a malformed quantized artifact to be published.
- Model publication did not include sufficient checksum validation or content validation for quant blocks.
- Alerting thresholds and escalation for canaries were not tuned for fast detection of perf regressions.

Immediate post-incident actions (already completed):
- Reverted CI packager to v1.11.8 pending root-cause fix (owner: Mei).
- Added an urgent verification step to the publication job that inspects weight headers for quant block presence (temporary script) (owner: Oliver).
- Backfilled artifact for the failed build and re-run performance preflight in staging (owner: Lena).

Longer-term remediation and runbook changes (owners and ETA):
1) CI: Fix race in packager to guarantee atomic assembly of quant blocks and fail the build instead of publishing a malformed artifact. (owner: Mei Chen, ETA: 2025-11-12)
2) Artifact validation: Add a mandatory artifact-content-validation stage in CI that verifies quant block checksums and asserts consistency between manifest flags and weight contents. Fail publishing if mismatch. (owner: Oliver Grant, ETA: 2025-11-08)
3) Runtime: Add a fast-weight-sanity-check at load time that can quickly validate presence of quant segments and fall back with a clear, paged alert if mismatch occurs (instead of a silent perf degradation). (owner: Runtime team, PR #2897) (ETA: 2025-11-18)
4) Alerting: Create per-canary latency escalation policies (p95) with lower thresholds and automatic paging to SRE on-call. (owner: SRE tooling, ETA: 2025-11-06)
5) Canary playbook: Update rollout runbook to require a synthetic preflight (small burst with representative short/long sequences) and require p50/p95 checks before traffic ramp beyond 5%. Add a mandatory 10-minute hold after canary start before automated ramp. (owner: SRE, ETA: 2025-11-07)
6) Model catalog: Require performance profile metadata for each model artifact (expected p50/p95 on standard microbench harness) and surface mismatch warnings during publication. (owner: Product infra, ETA: 2025-11-20)
7) Automation: Add automated rollback if canary p95 exceeds baseline by >2x for 5 minutes. (owner: Rollouts team, ETA: 2025-11-15)

Runbook excerpt (new steps to insert into canary playbook):
- Pre-deploy: Ensure artifact validation step completes successfully and CI returns content-verified: true.
- Deploy start: Allocate a dedicated canary pool and set traffic split to 5% (manual approve).
- Hold: Wait 10 minutes with synthetic preflight (run synthetic suite SRE-quick-perf). Evaluate p50 and p95; if p95 > baseline*1.5 -> abort and rollback.
- Monitor: Enable per-canary p95 alert and page SRE on-call if triggered.
- Auto-rollback: If automated rollback enabled, confirm rollback executed and validate stability for 30m before reattempt.

Checklist for on-call (short):
1) Pause rollout (if active).
2) Check kernel_selector logs for flags: "selected_unoptimized_path", "disabled_fused_attention", "quant_flag_mismatch".
3) Verify artifact manifest vs weight header (use scripts/inspect_weights.sh).
4) If mismatch: rollback to previous variant and drain canary nodes.
5) Scale nodes temporarily to relieve queueing if rollback will take >10m.
6) Open JIRA and tag runtime/ci teams.

Scripts/commands used in triage (examples):
- Inspect kernel selector logs:
  gcloud logging read "resource.labels.cluster_name=canary-us-west-2 AND textPayload:\"kernel_selector\"" --limit 200 --order=timestamp
- Quick inspect weights header:
  scripts/inspect_weights.sh gs://artifacts/redwood/packaged/redwood-rm-l2-quant-v2/17422/weights.bin | head -n 40
- Force rollback via rollout API:
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/rollouts/stop?deployment=canary-us-west-2

Follow-ups (owners assigned):
- Mei: fix packager race + add unit tests (ETA 2025-11-12).
- Oliver: permanent artifact validation + CI gating (ETA 2025-11-08).
- Runtime team: fast sanity-check + clearer paged error messages (ETA 2025-11-18).
- SRE: update canary playbook + add per-canary alerting (ETA 2025-11-07).
- Rollouts: implement auto-rollback policy (ETA 2025-11-15).

Lessons learned / notes:
- Relying solely on metadata flags without content validation creates a blind spot for performance regressions; we need content-aware publication.
- Canary isolation worked as designed; smaller canary thresholds and synthetic preflight would have caught this earlier.
- Runtime should surface a high-visibility, paged alert when the chosen execution path is the conservative/unoptimized one due to suspicious metadata.

Appendix: quick debug log excerpts (redacted):
[2025-11-03T09:27:12Z] kernel_selector: selected_unoptimized_path=true reason=quant_flag_mismatch model=redwood-rm-l2-quant-v2 node=canary-7
[2025-11-03T09:27:12Z] runtime.attention: disabled_fused_attention=true fallback=multi-kernel-launch
[2025-11-03T09:27:13Z] perf.batch: avg_batch_size=2.1 throughput_drop=0.67

If you have questions or want to push any remediation faster, ping #sre-canary and assign to the owners above.
